claims: Humiliation is the intense, painful experience of losing self-esteem, dignity, or status.
Humiliation is often caused by the unjust, public exercise of power by others.
Humiliation differs from shame by centering on being wronged rather than doing wrong.
Humiliation often causes a "freezing" trauma response.
Dr. Paul Gilbert's work on Compassion and Self-Compassion explains developing a compassionate, "compassionate self" identity (wise, strong, courageous) to counter feelings of worthlessness.
Humiliation is a tool used to demonstrate superiority.
Humiliation used to demonstrate superiority results in the exclusion or silencing of individuals or groups.
Humiliation is used historically as a public mechanism to punish wrongdoing.
Humiliation is used occasionally in modern times as a public mechanism to punish wrongdoing.
Public shaming is an example of humiliation used as a public mechanism to punish wrongdoing.
The Wikipedia article on Public humiliation shows public shaming.
